old: A deterministic canonical serialization gives the same provenance digest for identical records and, except for hash collisions, a different digest after any serialized field changes.
new: Fix a deterministic serialization $s$ and a deterministic hash function $h$. Identical serialized byte sequences have identical digests under $h$. Distinct serialized byte sequences have distinct digests unless they form a collision under $h$. Detecting a record change additionally requires that the change alter its serialized bytes.

old: Identical canonical byte sequences have identical images under the deterministic hash function. If two distinct byte sequences have the same hash, they form a collision by definition. Thus the first assertion is unconditional, while the change-detection assertion explicitly excludes that case. No injectivity of a fixed-length hash on arbitrary records is asserted.
new: If $s(r)=s(r')$, applying the function $h$ gives equal digests. If $s(r)\ne s(r')$ but $h(s(r))=h(s(r'))$, the two serialized strings form a hash collision by definition. Thus change detection at the record level requires both preservation of the audited distinction by $s$ and exclusion of a collision for the resulting bytes. No injectivity of a fixed-length hash on arbitrary byte strings is asserted.

old: \section{Correlated review}

Repeated refinement gives $R_0\preceq R_1\preceq\cdots\preceq R_d$ for the chosen recoverability tasks. More records need not give a strict gain for every task. Let $r_d\geq0$ be a declared unresolved-work score and $c_d\geq0$ the cumulative cost. These are model inputs. A small $r_d$ is not, without another theorem, a certificate of a nearly valid proof. The word cube names the layered presentation, not a cubical complex supplied with additional geometric axioms.
new:
A refinement preserves the certified target on its declared scope. Preservation of other tasks requires a separate recovery condition. Let $R_d:\mathscr A\to\mathcal R_d$ be the representation scheme at depth $d$. A sufficient condition is a map
\[
\pi_d:R_{d+1}(\mathscr A)\longrightarrow R_d(\mathscr A)
\qquad\text{with}\qquad R_d=\pi_d\circ R_{d+1}.
\]
If a task factors as $q=d_q\circ R_d$, then
\[
q=(d_q\circ\pi_d)\circ R_{d+1}.
\]
Hence $R_d\preceq_{\Qcal}R_{d+1}$. Repeated refinements satisfying this condition give the recoverability chain. For a restricted task family, preserving its supported tasks directly can suffice without recovering the entire preceding representation.

A longer derivation is not automatically a richer archive. It may reconstruct the same conclusion while omitting an example, a failed approach, or a provenance record. Those losses must be assessed against the declared task family.

Let $r_d\geq0$ be a declared unresolved-work score and $c_d\geq0$ the cumulative cost. These are model inputs. A small $r_d$ is not, without another theorem, a certificate of a nearly valid proof. The word cube names the layered presentation, not a cubical complex supplied with additional geometric axioms.

old: The main mathematical boundary is now clear. Verification is a closure property of the certified subfield. Discovery value belongs to a larger graph. Compression can preserve the first while reducing the second. Once that separation is formal, several consequences follow. Least certificate pairs can be extracted in fixed AND-DAGs. Alternative derivations create a genuine combinatorial optimization problem. Future-reach retention becomes submodular coverage. Version changes propagate through descendants. Correlated review has an effective sample size. Candidate generation is constrained by audit capacity. Expansion depth depends on purpose.
new:
The central distinction is between derivability within a declared inference system and the wider information retained by its archive. Certified closure records which claims follow from admitted leaves and accepted rules. Its interpretation as mathematical validity depends on the soundness of those leaves and rules. Discovery information serves different tasks: explaining a definition, locating a failed method, preserving a comparison, or opening a route to another problem.

Compression can preserve the present derivation while losing those other capabilities. Proof Path Theory makes that difference explicit through task families, recovery maps, extension problems, and versioned evidence. The certificate and the surrounding field should therefore be maintained together, with their logical roles kept distinct.

old: The review mean is unbiased only when its error means vanish.
new:
Endpoint equivalence fixes the complete assumption context. A refinement chain preserves the chosen tasks only when the corresponding recovery condition holds. The unrestricted positive-rule model always contains the full node set as a model. Nonempty global model spaces can still have empty prescribed extension fibers. Provenance change detection distinguishes information lost during serialization from collisions of different serialized bytes.

The review mean is unbiased only when its error means vanish.
